text:
College of Science, National Chengchi University
Guidelines for Subsidies for Overseas Study and International Activities
Approved by the 101st College Affairs Meeting on September 21, 2015
Amended and approved by the 130th College Affairs Meeting on September 18, 2023
1 The College of Science, National Chengchi University (hereinafter referred to as
"the College"), has established these guidelines to encourage students to engage in
short-term studies abroad or participate in international activities.
2 The international activities mentioned above include short-term studies, offsite
research, competitions, exhibitions, exchanges, attending conferences, and
presenting research output.
2.1 The definition of international activities shall be determined by the university's
Office of International Cooperation regulations.
2.2 Expense reimbursement shall comply with the regulations of the respective
funding source.
3 All students officially enrolled in the College are eligible to apply. In principle, each
individual may apply for one project per year. Applicants must submit their
applications within the deadlines announced by the College. Also, completing both
the submission of the return report and expense reimbursement within one month
after returning.
4 Applications will first undergo review by the applicant's unit supervisor. Once
approved, they will be submitted to the College's Administrative Supervisors'
Meeting, where the subsidy amounts and quotas will be determined based on the
budget and application status.
5 The priority order for granting incentives is as follows:
5.1 Based on the applicant's eligibility:
5.1.1 Domestic students from low- or middle-income households.
5.1.2 Domestic doctoral students.
5.1.3 Applicants who have not received other subsidies for the same purpose.
5.2 Based on the type of activity:
5.2.1 Applications from doctoral students participating in international activities
or engaging in short-term studies abroad will be prioritized.
5.2.2 If funding remains after subsiding the above activities, applications for
short-term studies abroad, field research, competitions, exhibitions,
exchanges, attending conferences, and presenting research findings may be
considered.
6 The maximum scholarship amount is NT$20,000 per person. The subsidy includes
round-trip airfare, living expenses, registration fees, and other related costs.
7 Required Application Documents:
7.1 Subsidy Application Form
7.2 Original and photocopy of documents proving the overseas activity (the
original will be returned after verification), such as proof of enrollment,
permission for studies, acceptance letters for international academic
conferences, invitation letters, conference agendas, or offsite research consent
forms.

7.3 Other supporting documents are beneficial for the evaluation.
8 Subsidy recipients who fail to complete their overseas plans as scheduled must
return the full amount of the scholarship. Exceptions apply to those who, due to
special circumstances, have received prior approval for a postponement. However, if
the overseas plan is not completed after one postponement, the full scholarship must
still be returned.
9 The priority for this guideline is to use external subsidy funds. Once these funds are
exhausted, the College's self-raised funds will be used. The annual subsidy limit for
the College's self-raised funds is NT$100,000.
10 This guideline is implemented after approval by the College Affairs Meeting and
issuance by the Dean. The same procedure applies for any amendments.

Article 1 The regulations is enacted in accordance with “ National Chengchi
University College of Science Regulations For Graduate Student
Scholarship and Bursaries ”.
Article 2 The College of Science (hereinafter referred to as "the College") establishes
a Graduate Scholarship Review Committee (hereinafter referred to as "the
Committee") to oversee scholarship review matters. The Committee
comprises the Dean and the heads of all departments and institutes as ex
officio members, along with one elected member from among the full-time
faculty of each department or institute. The Dean serves as the convener.
Committee members serve a one-year term and may be re-elected
consecutively.
Article 3 The graduate scholarships offered by the College are categorized into two
types: (1) Academic Paper Award and (2) Academic Excellence Award.
A student may receive both types of scholarships in the same semester.
For the Academic Paper Award, graduate students of the College may apply
if they have published a paper within the specified timeframe that has not
previously received the Academic Paper Award from the College.
Applications for the Academic Paper Award can be submitted once per
semester, with deadlines on March 31 and September 30, respectively. Only
papers published within one year prior to the application deadline are
eligible, and all application materials must be submitted by the announced
deadline (inclusive).
If the paper submitted for the Academic Paper Award has multiple authors,
all co-authors who wish to apply must submit a joint application. The
scholarship funds will be allocated among the eligible co-authors enrolled in
the College, based on their contributions, as determined by the Scholarship
Review Committee.
The review results and award recipient list must be compiled and submitted
to the university for approval within two months after the start of each
semester.
Article 4 The award review committee shall review academic paper awards based on
the following reward standards:

1. Papers published in journals indexed in SCI(E), SSCI, EI, or TSSCI:
NT$12,000 per paper.
2. Papers published in journals indexed in MR (Mathematical Reviews) or CIS
(Current Index to Statistics): NT$10,000 per paper.
3. Papers published in proceedings of international conferences indexed in
SCI(E) or EI: NT$6,000 per paper.
4. Papers presented at international conferences with an anonymous review
system or published in domestic and international journals with external
reviews (excluding the journals listed in the first and second categories):
NT$4,000 per paper.
5. Papers presented at domestic conferences with an anonymous review system:
NT$2,000 per paper.
6. Papers with other outstanding achievements will be discussed separately for
awards.
For papers published in journals, submission for award can be made once the paper is
indexed (including accepted papers). For conference papers, submission is only
accepted for those that have already been presented.
Before applying for the paper reward from the College, applicants must first apply for
funding or awards from the university’s R&D Office. If the funding exceeds the
College’s subsidy standards, no further application for the same paper can be made to
the College; if the funding is lower than the College's subsidy standards, the
difference will be supplemented based on the actual funding from the university’s
R&D Office.
Article 5 The number of recipients and the amount for the Excellent Academic
Performance Award each semester will be determined by each department, with a
principle of awarding no more than NT$15,000 and no less than NT$5,000 per
recipient. The total amount for each department’s excellent performance awards will
be allocated based on the department’s proportion of total graduate students, after
deducting the academic paper awards from the college’s allocated budget.
1. Publication of academic works and participation in academic conferences.
2. Academic performance (new students’ scores will be based on entrance exam
results).
3. Participation in department affairs and other special contributions.
The initial review results should be submitted to the College’s award review
committee for further review within one and a half months after the start of each
semester.
Article 6 Applicants for graduate student scholarships are limited to graduate students
of the College, excluding in-service master’s students, students on leave, and
exchange students.
Graduate student scholarships can be applied for once each semester, and applicants
must submit their applications within the designated timeframe.
Article 7 The College may retain 5% of the graduate student subsidy fund to assist
with research, teaching, and administrative tasks. The remaining funds will be
distributed to departments and institutes based on the ratio of the total number of

master’s and doctoral students.
When a department or institute organizes a national or international academic event,
they may apply to the College for graduate student work-study funding. The amount
of the subsidy will be determined by the dean based on the event's budget.
Article 8 The awarding of scholarships for in-service graduate students will be
handled according to the school’s regulations.
Article 9 Graduate student subsidies may be used to pay the learning allowances for
part-time learning assistants or wages for part-time labor assistants. Graduate students
may receive both types of support. Each college or department/institute should
establish their own rules for usage within the allocated budget.
The College must allocate at least 10% of the graduate student subsidy fund for
financial aid to low-income students.
For the purposes of this article, low-income students include those with proof of
being from a low-income household, proof of being from a middle-low-income
household, proof of being recognized as low-income by a village or town head, proof
of student loans, or those with specific circumstances demonstrating financial need.
Article 10 Graduate student subsidies must be provided in accordance with the
regulations outlined in the "National Chengchi University Student Part-time Assistant
and Temporary Personnel Utilization Announcement."
Article 11 Applicants for graduate student subsidies must be graduate students of the
College, excluding in-service graduate students, students on leave, and exchange
students. Applicants should submit their applications to the respective
department/institute within the designated timeframe.
Article 12 Graduate students receiving subsidies may also receive scholarships, but
they are not allowed to engage in full-time employment during the period they are
receiving subsidies. Violations of this rule will result in disqualification, and any
subsidies already received must be fully refunded.
Article 13 These regulations shall take effect upon approval by the College's
administrative meeting, and the same applies to any amendments.

Date 2021-11-09

Dear Teachers, Students and Friends of NCCU College of Science,

Glad to have you all here!

 

The NCCU College of Science is a special arrangement, but it has been rapidly become a favorable platform for multi-learning and interdisciplinary development. NCCU College of Science was established in 1994 as a separate major from Liberal Arts College. It retains the fine traditions of NCCU as well as the essence of humanistic care, natural exploration and the pursuit of truth. Unlike any general College of Science, our College uses scientific innovation and social contribution to emphasize the diverse development of humanities and society. Moreover, NCCU College of Science quality academic culture are excellent to cultivate and training many talents, high-level professional and management personnel for serving Society.

 

University education is the education of Man. It is one of the most direct methods to pursuit of highlight research talents, senior professional and management manpower. Since the industrial technology developed by basic science is extremely competitive, NCCU College of Science will constitute the best driving force for the development of the technology industry. On the other hand, globalization has had a huge impact on the function of universities, and university’s tasks are developing degree courses become more diversified capabilities. Not only education, lifelong education, distance education, but also other phased learning methods are constantly increasing. Teaching methods and research organization help students to receive higher education, which allows them to keep a balance between devotion from studying to searching. 

 

Furthermore, science and technology are developing at the speed of light, and our living conditions are also changing day by day. The Economist journal has specially pointed out the importance of lifelong learning and re-learning ability in this century. Our school is so proud of a strong foundation in the humanities field and internationally renowned. NCCU College of Science upholds the achievements of its predecessors, which combine relevant research on the existing basis while strive to contribution the foundation for future human civilization.

 

NCCU College of Science has three departments, two institutes and one university-level research center. Our College has been appointed academicians to prestigious research institutes within and beyond Taiwan such as: Academia Sinica (Taiwan) - International Postgraduate Doctorate Program in Swarm Networks and Human Intelligence Computing; Georgetown University (USA) - Double Degree in Bachelor and Master's degree of Electronic Physics degree; Counseling Master's degree program (School of Education); Digital Content and Technology/Master's degree program (Communication College); English-taught credit program (College of Science); Patent credit program (School of Law); Bachelor/Master of Mathematical Finance credit program (School of Business); Mathematical Information Credit Course; Mass Data Analysis Course (School of Business); Education Credit Course (School of Education); Language (School of Foreign Languages), Cognition and Brain Credit Course; Brain Science Credit Course. Combining with NCCU characteristics of the scientific spirit and practical methods to the fields of society, humanities, legal business, communication and social science integration, our College establish an academic leadership position in the integration of science and technology, humanities and social sciences. We will always advance the teaching and research in Scientific and Society areas.

 

有理走遍天下 – “Traveled the world to rational, irrational move an inch”

「理」 means that interesting, rigorous, and continuous. I will give you an example of three great predecessors as a conclusion: At the end of the 12th century, the Chinese master of Confucianism, Master Zhu Xi (朱熹) also mentioned "The Preface of Learning is Learning, Questioning, Thinking, and Discrimination, so does 「窮理致知」- Veritas et Conscientia is. About 500 years later, the West Copernicus published "The Theory of Celestial Movement" with dialectical thinking and discourse to subvert people's thinking at that time. I would like to remind you about the words of Greek philosopher Aristotle: “We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.”

 

Dean of College of Science

Dr. Hsing Luh

Regulations on the Use of Administrative Management Fees for Industry–
Academia Collaboration Projects
College of Science, National Chengchi University
Approved at the Administrative Supervisors Meeting of the College of Science on October 19, 2018
Article 1
These Regulations are established to ensure the proper use of administrative management
fees (hereinafter referred to as “the Fees”) derived from Ministry of Science and Technology
projects and industry–academia collaboration projects of the College, in accordance with the
“Regulations Governing the Implementation and Financial Management of Industry–
Academia Collaboration of National Chengchi University.”
Article 2
The administrative management fees allocated to the College each academic year shall be
centrally planned and utilized by the College for academic development purposes.
Article 3
The centrally managed Fees may be used for the following purposes:
1. Salaries of non-tenured personnel and additional compensation for full-time faculty
and research personnel beyond base salary and allowances.
2. Chair professorship funding, in accordance with the “Regulations for the
Establishment of Chair Professors of National Chengchi University.”
3. Teaching and research incentives and subsidies for faculty and research personnel.
4. Travel expenses for faculty and research personnel attending international
conferences, visits, training, or research activities as required for teaching and
research or by invitation.
5. Performance-based remuneration for administrative staff involved in industry–
academia collaboration, not exceeding 60% of their professional allowance per
month, subject to administrative approval by the President.
6. Expenses for hiring assistants, temporary staff, student workers, overtime pay, and
labor and health insurance.
7. Expenses for inviting domestic and international scholars and experts for lectures,
academic seminars, collaborative research, or experimental guidance.
8. Purchase of research equipment, books, consumables, and miscellaneous expenses
related to the College’s research and development.
9. Funding for support activities related to promoting industry–academia collaboration
(e.g., research exhibitions).
10. Necessary expenses for promoting the College’s research and development.
11. Other items consistent with the University’s regulations on industry–academia
collaboration and related to academic research.
Article 4
Expenditures of the Fees shall be reimbursed upon submission of supporting documents in
accordance with relevant University regulations.
Article 5
These Regulations shall be implemented upon approval by a College-level meeting; the same
shall apply to any amendments.

College of Science Regulations for the "Ministry of Education (MOE) Doctoral Scholarship"

Approved by the MOE Doctoral Scholarship Review Committee, College of Science, on December 23, 2024.

1. Eligibility: 

This scholarship is available to non-working doctoral students (Ph.D. students) in their first to third years who hold Republic of China (Taiwan) citizenship. The subsidy period begins from the date of approval until the end of the student's third year in the doctoral program. For those who graduate early, the award will be provided until the month of graduation.

2. Funding Breakdown: 

Each recipient receives a monthly stipend as follows:

MOE Subsidy: NT$20,000.

University Matching Fund: NT$15,000 (limited to newly admitted students).

College/Department Contribution:  * New Students: NT$5,000, Current Students: NT$20,000. 

(Note: The College/Department contribution may include the Cho-Cheng Scholarship, Teaching Assistant (TA) stipends, Research Assistant (RA) stipends, or NSTC personnel expenses such as research assistantships.)

3. Disqualification Criteria: 

Recipient status will be revoked if any of the following occur during the study period:

Failure to complete registration, taking a leave of absence, deferring enrollment, or withdrawing from the university.

Engaging in full-time employment in public or private institutions. (However, part-time work within university offices, serving as a part-time assistant for NSTC projects, or serving as a part-time lecturer is permitted. Any fraudulent claims will result in the MOE reclaiming the funds.)

Students fast-tracking to a Ph.D. program who transfer or return to a Master’s program.

Starting from the second semester after enrollment, if the previous semester's GPA falls below 80 or the conduct grade is lower than "A."

Concurrent receipt of the "National Science and Technology Council (NSTC) Doctoral Student Research Fellowship (Pilot Scheme)."

4. Student Responsibilities: 

Award recipients must assist with teaching or research-related tasks and other duties assigned by their advisors and departments, in accordance with the source of the matching funds.

5. Administrative Note: 

These regulations have been approved by the College of Science MOE Doctoral Scholarship Review Committee and are officially announced on the College website.

6. Evaluation and Continuation: 

Recipients are required to fill out a "Scholarship Continuation Evaluation Form" (defined by their respective departments) at the end of each semester. Supporting documents must be provided for departmental assessment. If a recipient fails to meet the College’s evaluation standards, they must undergo counseling; otherwise, their scholarship eligibility will be terminated.

Currently, the main focuses of the College are as follows:

Social Network and Service cross-disciplinary academic development

II. To implement the Elaboration Theory of Instruction and emphasize natural and liberal education

III. To provide comprehensive teaching resources and infrastructure as well as to expand academic resources

IV. To enhance the visibility and impact of the College of Science and all of its affiliated departments and institutes

V. To strengthen academic internationalization and global exchange

VI. To increase inter-college cooperation

Ideal

The College of Science of National Chengchi University fulfills the dual function of diversified learning and international perspective. It is our belief that active teaching and advanced research performed at our College is a guarantee of cultivating leadership talents in basic research, professionalism and humanistic care, and lays the foundation for employment and further development of students. The College of Science provides science & humanities trainings and high quality research so vital to improving student learning effectiveness, researching innovation and leading development in the age of international academic connections. Critical thinking and science continue to open up new academic value for the government, and return to the society with diversified academic development achievements. At the same time, students are guided to start the driving engine of lifelong learning, and then learn how to create their own value. 

 

Last but not least, likely Senior of National Chengchi University，Mr. Pu Ming said: "Learning is not a guarantee of surpassing others, but surpassing one's own kinetic energy."

title: （ENG）國立政治大學理學院(果夫樓、志希樓、大智樓)大樓 門禁管理作業實施要點.pdf
text:
Implementation Guidelines for Access Control Management
College of Science Buildings (Guofu Building, Zhixi Building, and Dazhi
Building), National Chengchi University
Amended and approved at the Administrative Coordination Meeting of the College of Science on September 14, 1999
Amended and approved at the Administrative Coordination Meeting of the College of Science on November 22, 2000
Amended and approved at the 21st College Affairs Meeting on December 12, 2000
Amended and approved at the 28th College Affairs Meeting on October 28, 2002
Amended and approved at the 48th College Affairs Meeting on December 8, 2005
Amended and approved at the 128th College Affairs Meeting on December 26, 2022
Article 1
To ensure the safety of the Guofu Building, Zhixi Building, and Dazhi Building of the
College of Science (hereinafter referred to as “the College”) and to facilitate access control
management, these Implementation Guidelines are hereby established.
Article 2
During non-working hours, access to the three buildings shall be controlled תועצמאב
electronic card access. The main entrances of the Guofu Building, Zhixi Building, and Dazhi
Building shall be managed by the College office.
Article 3
Faculty and staff of the College shall have access rights to the building where their affiliated
department is located and may apply for access to other buildings.
Master’s and doctoral students, research assistants, and undergraduate students who require
access for project courses may apply for access with approval from the heads of their
respective departments/institutes/programs. Unless special needs arise, access shall be limited
to the building where the applicant’s research or laboratory space is located.
Article 4
Application deadlines for access authorization:
Fall semester – September 30, October 31, November 30
Spring semester – March 31, April 30, May 31
Exceptions may be made under special circumstances.
Validity period of access authorization:
Faculty and staff – until the date of separation from employment.
Non-faculty personnel – two months after the end of the academic year of application.
Article 5
If an individual with access authorization lends their card to others, the College may revoke
their access privileges.
Article 6
The College is only responsible for setting access permissions on cards. Matters related to
issuance, damage, or loss of smart cards shall be handled directly with the issuing unit.
Article 7
These Implementation Guidelines shall be implemented upon approval by the College Affairs
Meeting; the same shall apply to any amendments.

Guidelines for the Establishment of the Curriculum Committee
College of Science, National Chengchi University
Approved at the 63rd College Affairs Meeting on June 15, 2009
Amended and approved at the 107th College Affairs Meeting on June 12, 2017
Amended and approved at the 120th College Affairs Meeting on September 21, 2020, Articles 2 and 4
Article 1
The College of Science, National Chengchi University (hereinafter referred to as “the
College”), in order to plan and develop curriculum-related matters, establishes the
“Curriculum Committee of the College of Science, National Chengchi University”
(hereinafter referred to as “the Committee”).
Article 2
The composition of the Committee is as follows:
(1) The Dean shall serve as an ex officio member and convener. Department, institute,
center, and degree program heads of the College shall serve as ex officio members,
along with one student representative. The student representative shall be elected
directly by students, with the election organized by student self-governing
bodies. Units with more than five full-time faculty members (excluding emeritus and
chair professors) may elect one additional faculty representative to serve as a member.
(2) When discussing major curriculum planning and revisions, one academic expert and
one industry representative from inside or outside the University may be appointed to
participate in the Committee.
(3) The term of office for ex officio members shall coincide with their term of office in
their respective positions. The student representative shall serve a one-year term,
while other members shall serve a two-year term; reappointment is permitted.
Article 3
The duties of the Committee are as follows:
(1) To integrate curriculum planning and design across departments, institutes, and
degree programs.
(2) To review all courses within the College; upon approval, such courses shall be
submitted to the University Curriculum Committee for recordation before
implementation.
(3) To carry out ad hoc tasks as assigned.
Article 4
Meetings of the Committee shall require the attendance of at least two-thirds of all members
to be valid; resolutions shall require the approval of more than half of the members present.
Members shall attend meetings in person. If unable to attend for valid reasons, a member may
appoint in writing another member from the same department, institute, center, or degree
program to attend and exercise voting rights on their behalf.
When proposals involve individual faculty evaluation, student representatives in
attendance shall recuse themselves to protect faculty privacy.

Article 5
Resolutions of the Committee shall be submitted to the College Affairs Meeting for
recordation.
Article 6
These Guidelines shall be implemented upon approval by the College Affairs Meeting; the
same shall apply to any amendments.

Regulations Governing the Formation of the Selection Committee for
Distinguished Professors and Distinguished Associate Professors
College of Science, National Chengchi University
Approved at the 72nd College Faculty Evaluation Committee Meeting on June 30, 2008
Approved by the President and implemented on July 8, 2008
Approved at the 190th College Faculty Evaluation Committee Meeting on March 24, 2022
Article 1
These Regulations are established in accordance with the Regulations and Implementation
Rules for the Appointment of Distinguished Professors and Distinguished Associate
Professors of National Chengchi University.
Article 2
The College of Science (hereinafter referred to as “the College”) shall establish a Selection
Committee (hereinafter referred to as the “College Selection Committee”) to nominate
candidates for Distinguished Professor and Distinguished Associate Professor positions and
to carry out the selection process.
Article 3
The College Selection Committee shall consist of five to nine members. The proportion
of external members (from outside the University or the College) shall not be less than
one-third of the total membership. The convener shall be elected by and from among
the members.
The Dean shall serve as an ex officio member. In addition, each department shall
nominate two senior distinguished professors, and each independent institute shall
nominate one senior distinguished professor as members. External members shall be
nominated by each department (at least one per department) and by independent
institutes on a rotating basis (at least one).
Members shall serve a one-year term and may be reappointed.
Any individual nominated as a candidate for Distinguished Professor shall not serve as
a member of the Committee.
Article 4
Meetings of the College Selection Committee shall be convened only when at least two-thirds
of all members are present.
Article 5
Minutes of the Committee’s selection meetings shall provide a detailed record of the review
process and explanations, and candidates shall be ranked in order of recommendation
priority. Before the end of May each year, the review materials for all candidates shall be
submitted confidentially to the University Chair Professor Appointment Committee for
review.
Article 6
Distinguished Professors and Distinguished Associate Professors may be reappointed upon
expiration of their term. For reappointment, each department or institute shall provide
evaluations on the candidate’s teaching, research, service performance, and fulfillment of
assigned duties during the appointment period, and submit them to the College Selection
Committee for review.

The Committee shall take into account the balanced allocation of new appointment quotas
and make a comprehensive assessment before submitting recommendations to the University
Chair Professor Appointment Committee in accordance with procedures.
Article 7
These Regulations shall be implemented upon approval by the College Faculty Evaluation
Committee; the same shall apply to any amendments.

National Chengchi University College of Science Regulations for
Implementation of Graduate Student Scholarships and Grants
Amended and approved at the 23rd College Affairs Meeting on June 15, 2001

9

Article 1
These regulations are established in accordance with the "National Chengchi University
Regulations for Implementation of Graduate Student Scholarships and Grants."
Article 2
The College of Science (hereinafter referred to as "the College") shall establish the Graduate
Scholarship Review Committee (hereinafter referred to as the "Review Committee") to
handle scholarship review matters.
The Review Committee consists of the Dean and the heads of each department/institute as ex-
officio members. Additionally, one faculty member shall be elected from each
department/institute to serve as a member. The Dean shall serve as the convener. Members
serve a one-year term and are eligible for re-election.
Article 3
Scholarships in this College are divided into two categories:
1. Academic Paper Awards
2. Outstanding Academic Performance Awards
The same individual may receive both types of scholarships in the same semester.
Academic Paper Awards:
• Graduate students of the College who publish papers within the specified timeframe
that have not previously received a paper award from the College may apply.
• Applications are accepted twice per academic year (once per semester), with cutoff
dates of March 31 and September 30, and are limited to papers published within the
previous year.

• Submissions must be made by the announced deadline.
• If a paper has multiple authors, all eligible applicants should apply together; the prize
money will be distributed among current student co-authors within the College by the
Review Committee based on their level of contribution.
• The review results and award list shall be submitted to the University for approval
within two months of the start of each semester.
Article 4
The Review Committee reviews Academic Paper Awards based on the following standards:
Award Amount
Category Publication Venue
(per paper)
Papers published in journals indexed in SCI(E), SSCI, EI, or
I NT$12,000
TSSCI.
Papers published in journals indexed in MR (Mathematical
II NT$10,000
Reviews) or CIS (Current Index to Statistics).
International conference papers indexed in SCI(E) or
III NT$6,000
EI proceedings.
International conference papers with an anonymous review
IV system or domestic/international journals with external review NT$4,000
(excluding categories I and II).
Domestic conference papers with an anonymous review
V NT$2,000
system.
Other outstanding achievements in paper publication (to be
VI TBD
discussed separately).
• Journal papers may be applied for once they are accepted or published.
• Conference papers are only eligible for application after they have been published.
• Prior Application Rule: Before applying to the College, students must first apply for
subsidies or awards from the University's Office of Research and Development. If
the University's award exceeds the College's standard, no further application to the
College is permitted. If it is lower, the College will cover the difference.
Article 5
The number of recipients and the amount for Outstanding Academic Performance
Awards are determined by each department. In principle, awards range from NT5,000
to NT15,000 per person. Total funding is based on the remaining University-allocated funds
after deducting Academic Paper Awards, distributed to departments based on the ratio of
Master’s and Doctoral students.
Criteria include:
1. Publication of academic works and participation in academic seminars.
2. Academic performance (new students are judged by entrance exam results).
3. Participation in department/institute affairs and other special contributions.

Preliminary results must be submitted to the College Review Committee for second-round
review within 1.5 months of the semester's start.
Article 6
Scholarship applicants are limited to graduate students of this
College. This excludes Executive Master's Program (on-the-job) students, students on leave,
and exchange students. Applications must be submitted to the College within the prescribed
timeframe once per semester.
Article 7
The College may reserve 5% of the Graduate Student Grant fund to assist in research,
teaching, and administrative promotion. The remainder is allocated to departments/institutes
based on a ratio (3x for Master's students, 4x for Doctoral students).
Article 8
Departments/institutes hosting national or international academic activities may apply for
student work-study grant subsidies, the amount of which is decided by the Dean based on the
budget.
Article 9
Grants for Executive Master's students follow University regulations. Grants may be used for
learning stipends (Learning-oriented assistants) or salaries (Labor-oriented assistants), and
students may receive both.
At least 10% of the Graduate Student Grant funds must be allocated for students in
financial hardship.
This includes those with low-income certificates, mid-to-low-income certificates,
village/neighborhood head certificates of hardship, student loan certifications, or other
concrete evidence of hardship.
Article 10
Employment must follow the University’s "Public Notice for Student Part-time Assistants
and Temporary Manpower."
Article 11
Grant applicants are limited to graduate students of the College, excluding Executive
Master's (on-the-job) students, students on leave, and exchange students.
Article 12
Grant recipients may concurrently receive scholarships. However, they must not hold full-
time paid employment while receiving a grant. Violators will be disqualified and must
return all received funds.

Article 13
These regulations shall take effect after being passed by the College Administrative Meeting;
the same applies to any amendments.

text:
Guidelines for the Selection of the Dean
College of Science, National Chengchi University
Approved by the College of Science Preparatory Committee on July 13, 1994
Amended and approved at the 1st College Affairs Meeting on October 19, 1994
Ratified at the 81st University Affairs Meeting on November 19, 1994
Amended and approved at the 2nd College Affairs Meeting on December 28, 1994
Amended and approved at the 10th College Affairs Meeting on January 6, 1997
Ratified at the 94th University Affairs Meeting on January 18, 1997
Amended and approved at the 28th College Affairs Meeting on October 28, 2002
Amended and approved at the 120th University Affairs Meeting on November 23, 2002
Amended and approved at the 59th College Affairs Meeting on September 24, 2008
Amended and approved at the 60th College Affairs Meeting on December 9, 2008, Article 11
Approved by the President on December 29, 2008
Amended and approved at the 62nd College Affairs Meeting on May 4, 2009, title and Articles 1 and 13
Amended and approved at the 63rd College Affairs Meeting on June 15, 2009, Articles 4, 6, and 10
Ratified at the 156th University Affairs Meeting on November 21, 2009
Amended and approved at the 69th College Affairs Meeting on June 3, 2010
Reorganized into formal regulations in accordance with the resolution of the 159th University Affairs Meeting on June 29,
2010
Amended and approved at the 79th College Affairs Meeting on April 16, 2012
Ratified at the 169th University Affairs Meeting on June 25, 2012
Article 1.
These Guidelines are established by the College of Science, National Chengchi University
(hereinafter referred to as “the College”), in accordance with the University’s Regulations for
the Selection of Deans.
Article 2.
The Dean shall be a professor with administrative competence and a strong commitment to
service, appointed concurrently. The term of office is three years, and one consecutive
reappointment is permitted.
Article 3.
A Selection Committee (hereinafter referred to as the “Committee”) shall be formed and
convened by the University to conduct the selection process four months prior to the
expiration of the Dean’s term or within two months after a vacancy occurs.
Article 4.
The Committee shall consist of eleven members as follows:
(1) Seven faculty representatives elected by the College Affairs Meeting. Candidates may
be nominated by departments (institutes) or self-nominated, and elected by vote; each
department (institute) shall have at least one representative. Alternate members in
equal number shall also be elected and ranked by unit.
(2) Two external academic or professional experts, recommended by departments
(institutes), with four candidates elected by the College Affairs Meeting and
submitted to the President for final selection.
(3) Two members appointed by the President.
The convener of the Committee shall be designated by the President, and administrative
support shall be provided by the Office of Personnel.

Article 5.
Candidates for Dean shall be nominated as follows:
(1) Each department (institute) may recommend up to one candidate through its
departmental meeting.
(2) Self-nomination is permitted.
The Committee may also nominate candidates with the endorsement of at least one-third of
its members before the application deadline.
Article 6.
The Committee may, when necessary, organize presentations or forums for Dean candidates.
Article 7.
The Committee may convene meetings only when at least two-thirds of its members are
present. Resolutions require the approval of more than half of the members present. Members
must attend in person and may not appoint proxies.
Article 8.
The Committee shall carry out its duties with fairness and independence, and shall vote on
each candidate individually by secret ballot.
When a candidate receives approval from more than half of the members present, the
candidate meets the nomination threshold, and vote counting shall cease. Ballots shall be
sealed and submitted to the President for reference.
Candidates meeting the threshold shall be listed in order of stroke count of their names, along
with detailed personal information and specific reasons for recommendation, and submitted
to the President for final appointment.
Article 9.
If the Committee fails to complete the selection process one month before the end of the
Dean’s term, it may extend the selection period, which shall not exceed six months from the
date of its first meeting. During the extension period, to ensure continuity of administration,
the President may appoint an acting Dean.
If none of the recommended candidates is appointed by the President, a new Committee shall
be formed in accordance with Article 4 to restart the selection process.
Article 10.
If the Dean is eligible for reappointment upon the expiration of the term, the President shall
decide on reappointment five months in advance after considering relevant college
regulations, the willingness of the incumbent, performance in advancing college affairs,
alignment with university development needs, and opinions from within the College.
Administrative support for the reappointment process shall be provided by the Office of
Personnel, with assistance from the Election Study Center and the College.
Article 11.
If special circumstances arise during the Dean’s term, a motion of no confidence may be
proposed by the President or by more than half of the representatives of the College Affairs
Meeting. The Vice President shall convene the College Affairs Meeting, and upon approval
by at least two-thirds of all representatives, the President may remove the Dean from office.
A new Selection Committee shall then be formed in accordance with regulations.

Article 12.
Under any of the following circumstances, the President shall appoint a qualified professor as
Acting Dean, whose term shall last until a new Dean assumes office, but not exceeding one
year:
(1) Resignation or vacancy of the incumbent Dean pending a new selection.
(2) Re-selection pursuant to Article 9, Paragraph 2.
(3) Removal from office pursuant to Article 11 and pending a new selection.
Article 13.
These Guidelines shall be implemented upon approval by the College Affairs Meeting and
ratification by the University Affairs Meeting; the same shall apply to any amendments.
The amendments ratified on June 25, 2012 shall take effect on August 1, 2012.

Article 1
These Guidelines are established in accordance with Article 14 of the Regulations Governing
the Establishment of the Faculty Evaluation Committee of National Chengchi University..
Article 2
The College Faculty Evaluation Committee (hereinafter referred to as the “College FEC”)
shall review the following matters:
(1) Qualifications, rank, and term of appointment of faculty members.
(2) Promotion and change of appointment of faculty members.
(3) Dismissal, suspension, and non-renewal of appointment of faculty members.
(4) Determination of eligibility for extension of service and grounds for severance.
(5) Conferment of emeritus professor titles.
(6) Other matters that shall be reviewed in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.
Resolutions of the College FEC on the above matters (second-level review) shall be
submitted to the University Faculty Evaluation Committee for final review.
Separate regulations shall be established for faculty appointment and promotion review
procedures of the College.
Article 3
The College FEC shall consist of no fewer than nine members, including ex officio members
and elected members.
The Dean shall serve as an ex officio member. In addition, each department shall elect three
full professors, and each institute shall elect one full professor to serve as members.
When necessary, elected members may be professors from outside the College.
The Dean shall serve as the convener; however, if recusal is required, one member shall be

elected by and from among the members to act as convener.
Members shall serve a one-year term and may be re-elected. Vacancies shall be filled by
supplementary election from the respective department or institute.
Article 4
The College FEC shall convene at least once each semester and may hold special meetings
when necessary.
A meeting shall require the attendance of more than half of all members to be valid;
resolutions shall require the approval of at least two-thirds of the members present. Members
who must recuse themselves shall not be counted in the quorum for that case. Relevant
personnel may be invited to attend and provide reports or explanations when necessary.
Matters concerning dismissal, suspension, or non-renewal of faculty shall comply with the
quorum and voting requirements stipulated in the applicable Teacher Act.
For faculty promotion cases, at least two-thirds of all members must be present, and decisions
shall be made through a two-stage secret ballot process as follows:
(1) Upon confirmation that the applicant meets the promotion requirements stipulated in the
College’s faculty appointment and promotion guidelines, at least two-thirds of the attending
members must approve submission of the representative works and relevant materials for
external review.
(2) Upon passing the external review, at least two-thirds of the attending members shall
approve through a review and scoring process, after which the case shall be submitted to the
University FEC for final review.
Article 5
Members of the College FEC shall attend meetings in person. A member who is absent
without justification for two consecutive meetings shall be deemed to have forfeited
membership, and an alternate member shall fill the vacancy in order.
Article 6
When reviewing cases, a member shall recuse himself or herself if the member, or the
member’s spouse, former spouse, blood relative within the fourth degree, or relative by
marriage within the third degree, is a party to the case.
If a member has other conflicts of interest and fails to recuse voluntarily, the College FEC
may resolve to require recusal.
If a member believes there are other special circumstances requiring recusal, the member may
apply to the College FEC.
If there are concrete facts indicating possible bias, the concerned party may request the
recusal of a member and shall provide reasons and supporting facts.
Recusal applications under the preceding two paragraphs shall be decided by the College
FEC.

Article 7
If the College FEC overturns a case already approved by a department, institute, or degree
program FEC, it shall notify the relevant unit of the reasons for disapproval.
Article 8
For matters concerning faculty qualifications, term of appointment, promotion, dismissal,
suspension, non-renewal, extension of service, determination of severance grounds, or other
matters required by law to be reviewed—if the facts are clear and the
department/institute/degree program FEC fails to act or its resolution violates applicable
regulations, the College FEC may directly review or revise the case in accordance with
regulations.
Article 9
Any matters not covered by these Guidelines shall be handled in accordance with the relevant
regulations of the University.
Article 10
These Guidelines shall be implemented after being passed by the College Council and
submitted to the University Faculty Evaluation Committee for record; the same applies to any
future amendments.

Organizational Regulations for the College Affairs Meeting,
College of Science, National Chengchi University
Approved at the 1st College Affairs Meeting on October 19, 1994
Amended and approved at the 6th College Affairs Meeting on December 20, 1995
Ratified at the 88th University Affairs Meeting on January 13, 1996
Following the amendment to Article 43 of the University Organizational Regulations at the 129th University Affairs Meeting
on June 10, 2004, Article 10 of these Regulations was automatically revised accordingly

Article 1
The College of Science of National Chengchi University (hereinafter referred to as “the
College”) establishes the College Affairs Meeting (hereinafter referred to as “the Meeting”)
in accordance with Article 43 of the University’s Organizational Regulations.
Article 2
The Meeting is the highest decision-making body of the College. It consists of the Dean,
Associate Dean(s), department chairs, institute directors, representatives of full-time faculty
members, and student representatives. The Dean serves as the chairperson and convenes
discussions on major college affairs. When necessary, adjunct faculty, teaching assistants,
staff, students, and other relevant persons may be invited to attend as non-voting participants.
Article 3
Full-time faculty representatives shall be elected separately by each department and each
institute, with two representatives from each department and one from each institute. The
term of office is one year, and re-election is permitted.
Article 4
Two student representatives shall be elected directly by students, with elections organized by
student self-governing bodies.
Their term of office is one year, and re-election is permitted.
Article 5
The Meeting shall be convened and chaired by the Dean at least once each semester. If the
Dean is unable to preside, an acting representative shall do so.
The Dean may convene extraordinary meetings when necessary. If more than one-third of the
College’s full-time faculty jointly request an extraordinary meeting, the Dean shall convene it
within ten days.
Article 6
The Meeting shall deliberate on the following matters:
1. Development policies and plans of the College.
2. Important regulations of the College.
3. Proposals submitted to the Meeting and matters referred by the Dean.

4. Resolutions made by committees or task forces established under the Meeting.
5. Other matters concerning the College as a whole.
Article 7
Proposals to the Meeting may be submitted by:
1. The Dean.
2. Departments or institutes.
3. Full-time faculty members, administrative staff, or students, with the joint
endorsement of at least two Meeting representatives.
All proposals must be submitted in written form to the College office at least one week
prior to the Meeting. The proposing unit or relevant individuals shall attend the
Meeting to provide explanations.
Article 8
The Meeting may establish various committees or task forces to handle matters assigned by
the Meeting.
Article 9
The Meeting may be convened only when more than half of all representatives are present.
Resolutions require the approval of more than half of those present. Non-voting attendees do
not have voting rights.
Article 10
These regulations shall be implemented after being approved by the Meeting and filed with
the Administrative Meeting. The same procedure applies to any amendments.

Article 1.
The College of Science, National Chengchi University (hereinafter referred to as “the
College”), in order to enhance teaching quality and to recognize and commend faculty
members for outstanding contributions to teaching, hereby establishes these Implementation
Guidelines in accordance with the University’s Regulations for the Incentive Program for
Outstanding Teaching Faculty (hereinafter referred to as “the Guidelines”).
Article 2.
To conduct the selection of Outstanding Teaching Faculty, the College shall establish a
Selection Committee (hereinafter referred to as the “College Selection Committee”).
Members of the College Selection Committee shall be concurrently appointed from among
the members of the College Faculty Evaluation Committee. Any member nominated as a
candidate for Outstanding Teaching Faculty shall recuse themselves from the review process
for that academic year.
Article 3.
Meetings of the College Selection Committee shall require the attendance of at least two-
thirds of all members in person to be valid; resolutions shall require the approval of more
than half of the members present.
Article 4.
The selection for Outstanding Teaching Faculty shall be conducted once each academic year,
following the procedures below:
(1) Data collection stage:
1. The Office of Academic Affairs shall provide a list of courses ranking within the top
40% in teaching evaluation results (both semesters of the previous academic year) for
each college and department/institute.
2. The Office of Personnel, in collaboration with the Computer Center, shall conduct a
questionnaire survey on Outstanding Teaching Faculty and provide a list of faculties
ranking within the top 50% in each college and department/institute, as well as those
who have passed the annual faculty performance evaluation.
(2) Nomination stage by the College Selection Committee:
1. Upon receiving the above data, the College shall forward the relevant information to
each department/institute for reference.
2. Each department/institute shall, based on the above data and the following criteria
(with supporting documentation), nominate and rank candidates, and submit
nomination forms and related materials to the College Selection Committee for
review. In principle, each department may nominate up to two candidates and each

institute one candidate:
(1) Demonstrates and effectively implements teaching philosophy with outstanding
results.
(2) Develops teaching materials or websites, innovates teaching methods, and
compiles them into textbooks with excellent outcomes for peer reference.
(3) Inspires students’ interest in learning and encourages study and reading with
notable results.
(4) Provides regular student guidance and fosters motivation for learning with positive
outcomes.
(5) Achieves outstanding teaching performance recognized by peer evaluation;
teaching observation panels may be formed if necessary.
(6) Enhances professional competencies with outstanding results.
(7) Distribution of student performance outcomes.
(8) Effective use of digital teaching materials, websites, and instructional media.
(9) Supervises undergraduate research projects funded by the Ministry of
Science and Technology and engages in industry-academia collaboration with
excellent outcomes.
(10) Other relevant teaching-related materials.
3. After comprehensive review, the College Selection Committee shall nominate up to
twice the number of available awards, rank the candidates, and submit the nomination
forms and supporting materials to the University Outstanding Teaching Faculty
Selection Committee for final review.
Article 5.
Faculty members who have not passed the University’s performance evaluation and have
been filed for record by the University Faculty Evaluation Committee shall not be eligible for
selection.
Article 6.
Faculty members receiving the Distinguished Teaching Award subsidy during the award
period shall not participate in the selection.
Article 7.
Matters not covered herein shall be handled in accordance with the University’s Regulations
for the Incentive Program for Outstanding Teaching Faculty and other relevant laws and
regulations.
Article 8.
These Guidelines shall be implemented upon approval by the College Affairs Meeting and
filing for record with the University Selection Committee; the same shall apply to any
amendments.

title: （ENG）國立政治大學理學院建教合作計畫行政管理費使用辦法 .pdf
text:
Regulations on the Use of Administrative Management Fees for Industry–
Academia Collaboration Projects
College of Science, National Chengchi University
Approved at the Administrative Supervisors Meeting of the College of Science on October 19, 2018
Article 1
These Regulations are established to ensure the proper use of administrative management
fees (hereinafter referred to as “the Fees”) derived from Ministry of Science and Technology
projects and industry–academia collaboration projects of the College, in accordance with the
“Regulations Governing the Implementation and Financial Management of Industry–
Academia Collaboration of National Chengchi University.”
Article 2
The administrative management fees allocated to the College each academic year shall be
centrally planned and utilized by the College for academic development purposes.
Article 3
The centrally managed Fees may be used for the following purposes:
1. Salaries of non-tenured personnel and additional compensation for full-time faculty
and research personnel beyond base salary and allowances.
2. Chair professorship funding, in accordance with the “Regulations for the
Establishment of Chair Professors of National Chengchi University.”
3. Teaching and research incentives and subsidies for faculty and research personnel.
4. Travel expenses for faculty and research personnel attending international
conferences, visits, training, or research activities as required for teaching and
research or by invitation.
5. Performance-based remuneration for administrative staff involved in industry–
academia collaboration, not exceeding 60% of their professional allowance per
month, subject to administrative approval by the President.
6. Expenses for hiring assistants, temporary staff, student workers, overtime pay, and
labor and health insurance.
7. Expenses for inviting domestic and international scholars and experts for lectures,
academic seminars, collaborative research, or experimental guidance.
8. Purchase of research equipment, books, consumables, and miscellaneous expenses
related to the College’s research and development.
9. Funding for support activities related to promoting industry–academia collaboration
(e.g., research exhibitions).
10. Necessary expenses for promoting the College’s research and development.
11. Other items consistent with the University’s regulations on industry–academia
collaboration and related to academic research.
Article 4
Expenditures of the Fees shall be reimbursed upon submission of supporting documents in
accordance with relevant University regulations.
Article 5
These Regulations shall be implemented upon approval by a College-level meeting; the same
shall apply to any amendments.

The College of Science was founded in 1994 from the former College of Arts and Sciences. The College of Science is now made up three departments, two graduate institutes and seven research centers & programs. The scope of research covers the entire range of basic sciences and social sciences, which represented by the Department of Mathematical Sciences, Department of Psychology, and the Department of Computer Science, as well as the Graduate Institute of Neuroscience and the Graduate Institute of Applied Physics.

Seven Centers & Programs are currently housed in the College also: the Research Center for Mind, Brain and Learning, Master Program in Digital Content and Technologies (in conjunction with the College of Communication), Patents Course Program (co-founded with the College of Law in 2010), MA Program of Counseling and Guidance (co-founded with the College of Education in 2011), Bachelor Program in Digital Content and Technologies (co-founded with the College of Communication in 2011), and the Financial Mathematics Program (co-founded with the College of Commerce in 2011). In 2012, together with the College of Foreign Languages and Literature, the international and pioneering cross-disciplinary Language, Cognition and Brain Program was established. In 2014, the Social Networks and Human-Centered Computing (SNHCC) Ph.D. Program was founded in joint collaboration with the Department of Computer Science, Academia Sinica, and National Tsing Hua University.

National Chengchi University – College of Science
Reiteration of Regulations and Operational Principles for Processing Faculty Promotion
Applications
Retention Period: —
Address: No. 64, Sec. 2, Zhinan Rd., Wenshan District, Taipei City
Fax: 2936-0360
Contact Person: Liao, Ting-Chun
Telephone: 02-29393091 ext. 62042
Recipient: As designated units
Date of Issue: November 16, 2009
Document No.:政院理校字第0980024232號
Urgency Level: Ordinary
Classification and Declassification Conditions / Confidentiality Period: Ordinary
Attachments:
1. Department Chair’s Endorsement Form
2. Ranking List of Faculty Members Applying for Promotion to the Same Rank
Subject：Reiteration of the relevant regulations and operational principles for processing faculty
promotion applications in the College. Please be informed and comply accordingly.
Explanation：
1. This matter is handled in accordance with the resolution adopted at the 84th meeting of the
College Faculty Review Committee.
2. The important regulations and operational principles regarding the College’s acceptance of
faculty promotion applications are listed as follows:
(1) Each department/institute shall conduct a substantive review of its faculty members’
promotion applications before submitting them to the College Faculty Review Committee for
deliberation. If the submitted materials fail to comply with relevant requirements (e.g., lack of
proof regarding journal classification), the application will be returned and not processed.
(2) According to the latter part of Article 13 of the University’s Regulations for Faculty
Appointment and Promotion Review:
“For representative works co-authored with others, the applicant must indicate their contribution
in that work and obtain signed certification from the co-authors. Additionally, works authored
solely by the applicant must be attached.”
Therefore, if the representative work submitted by the applicant is not a single-authored work,
they must also submit other single-authored works in order for the Faculty Review Committee to
accept the application for deliberation.
(3) When a department submits faculty promotion applications to the College Faculty Review

Committee for deliberation, it shall attach a Department Chair’s Endorsement Form (see
Attachment 1), providing a comprehensive evaluation of the applicant’s performance in various
aspects for the Committee’s reference.
If a department submits two or more applications for promotion to the same rank at the same
time, it must prepare a Ranking List of Faculty Members Applying for Promotion to the
Same Rank (see Attachment 2).
(4) Article 4, Paragraph 2 of the College’s “Operational Guidelines for Faculty Appointment and
Promotion” stipulates the method of calculating points for different types of academic works.
Since certain provisions have been subject to varying interpretations, the meanings are hereby
confirmed as follows:
1. Works counted on a per-article basis:
● Journal articles with anonymous peer review (Category 1)
● Book chapters (Category 4)
2. Works counted on a total-volume basis:
● Conference papers (Category 2)
● Complete books (Category 3)
In this part, the Department Faculty Review Committee shall propose a recommended
point value, and the College Faculty Review Committee shall approve a total score
between 2 to 6 points.
3. For patents (Category 5), one related paper may be additionally counted toward the total
points; however, the maximum cumulative score is capped at 6 points.
Implementation: Henceforth, when departments submit faculty promotion applications to the
College Faculty Review Committee for deliberation, they must first verify that all required
documents are complete in accordance with the above explanation.
If the applicant meets the eligibility criteria but has omitted required documents, the department
should remind the applicant to supplement the application materials in accordance with the
relevant regulations. The completed applications shall then be submitted within the deadlines
(before the end of April and the end of October each year) to the University Faculty Review
Committee for preliminary review and approval, and subsequently to the College Faculty Review
Committee for deliberation.
Original:
Department of Mathematical Sciences, Department of Psychology, Department of Computer Science,
Institute of Neuroscience, Institute of Applied Physics

Key Points for Faculty Appointment and Promotion Evaluation Procedures, College of Science, National
Chengchi University
Approved at the 28th College Affairs Meeting on October 28, 2002
Ratified at the 205th University Faculty Evaluation Committee Meeting on January 22, 2003
Amended at the 30th College Affairs Meeting on March 13, 2003 (Article 7)
Ratified at the 210th University Faculty Evaluation Committee Meeting on July 16, 2003
Amended at the 42nd College Affairs Meeting on June 15, 2004 (Article 6)
Amended at the 43rd College Affairs Meeting on October 28, 2004 (Article 2)
Ratified at the 224th University Faculty Evaluation Committee Meeting on November 24, 2004
Amended at the 51st College Affairs Meeting on June 13, 2006 (Article 4)
Ratified at the 243rd University Faculty Evaluation Committee Meeting on October 25, 2006
Amended at the 69th College Affairs Meeting on June 3, 2010 (Articles 4–8)
Amended at the 73rd College Affairs Meeting on December 27, 2010

Ratified at the 352nd University Faculty Evaluation Committee Meeting on May 23, 2018
