Ratified at the 364th University Faculty Evaluation Committee Meeting on November 27, 2019
Amended at the 126th College Affairs Meeting on April 25, 2022 (Articles 2, 8 & 8-1)
Ratified at the 384th University Faculty Evaluation Committee Meeting on May 11, 2022
— Article 2 effective upon ratification; other amendments effective June 1, 2022 —
Amended at the 131st College Affairs Meeting on December 25, 2023 (Articles 2, 4 & 7)
Ratified at the 399th University Faculty Evaluation Committee Meeting on April 17, 2024
Article 1
The College of Science (hereinafter “the College”) of National Chengchi University (hereinafter “the
University”) establishes these Key Points in accordance with Article 27 of the University Regulations for
Faculty Appointment and Promotion Evaluation to govern the appointment and promotion procedures of
faculty members within the College.
Article 2
New full-time faculty appointments shall be limited to the rank of lecturer or above.
Appointment to assistant professor or higher ranks shall, in principle, require a doctoral degree and
relevant experience demonstrating teaching and research capability.
Part-time appointments are limited to special teaching needs.
New faculty who already possess a Ministry of Education–approved teaching certificate may be
appointed according to the certificate rank.
For full-time appointees without an equivalent-level teaching certificate, qualification review shall follow
the Ministry of Education Regulations for Faculty Qualification Review for Junior Colleges and Above.

For diploma-based appointment cases, the department/institute/program shall submit the case for review
by at least three external scholars or experts authorized by the College.When reviewed by three
reviewers, the result shall be deemed passed if all three are rated “C” or higher and at least two are rated
“B” or higher; When reviewed by more than three reviewers, the pass threshold shall not be lower than
the above standard.
For non–diploma-based appointments, the external review process shall follow the same rules as those
for promotion (as in Article 7, Item 5).
If the College Faculty Evaluation Committee questions the external reviewers’ results, it shall handle the
matter in accordance with Article 39 of the Regulations for Faculty Qualification Review for Junior
Colleges and Above.
Article 3
When applying for promotion, the applicant’s representative works shall be evaluated according to the
scoring standards established by the respective department/institute/program and relevant College
regulations.
The departmental Faculty Evaluation Committee shall preliminarily calculate points based on Article 5
and conduct a substantive review before submitting the case to the College Committee.
If the materials do not comply with relevant regulations, the College may reject and return the
application.
The application should include the department chair’s comprehensive written comments on the
applicant’s performance in all aspects for reference by the College Committee.
If multiple faculty members of the same rank apply simultaneously, their cases shall be ranked in order of
recommendation.
Article 4
Applicants’ scholarly works for promotion must meet the following requirements:
1. Representative works must be produced after acquiring the previous faculty rank and within five
years prior to the effective date of promotion.
Reference works must be within seven years before the effective date.
Applicants who were pregnant or gave birth during this period may extend the time limits by two
years.
2. Scholarly works must be: Published monographs (with proof of publication), or articles published
in recognized academic journals (or officially accepted for publication with certification).
All works must relate to the applicant’s teaching field and comply with Ministry of Education
regulations.
3. For coauthored representative works, the applicant must specify their contribution, and all
coauthors must sign a statement waiving their right to use the work for future review.
4. Works that are part of a related series may be presented as a group with explanatory notes.
Accepted-but-unpublished works must be published within one year from acceptance. If publication is
delayed due to reasons beyond the applicant’s control, an extension may be applied for, up to three
years from the acceptance date.

Once the applicant obtains a higher-rank teaching certificate, the same work cannot be reused in future
promotions.
Article 5 – Scoring of Promotion Works
1. Peer-reviewed journal articles
○ Level 1: Scholarly articles published in journals indexed in SCI(E), SSCI, EI, or TSSCI, or
other scholarly journals recognized by the College Faculty Evaluation Committee, shall
be awarded six (6) points per article.
○ Level 2: Scholarly articles published in other academic journals with an external
peer-review system shall be awarded two (2) points per article.
2. Academic Conference papers — Proof of blind peer review shall be provided, or the papers shall
be evaluated by the College Faculty Evaluation Committee. Points shall be calculated on an
aggregate basis, with a total of two (2) to six (6) points determined by the College Faculty
Evaluation Committee based on the points recommended by the Department Faculty
Evaluation Committee.
3. Books (monographs) — Proof of blind peer review shall be provided, or the work shall be
evaluated by the College Faculty Evaluation Committee. Points shall be calculated on an
aggregate basis, with a total of two (2) to six (6) points determined by the College Faculty
Evaluation Committee based on the points recommended by the Department Faculty Evaluation
Committee.
4. Book chapters — Proof of blind peer review shall be provided, or the work shall be evaluated by
the College Faculty Evaluation Committee. One (1) point shall be awarded per chapter, with a
maximum cumulative total of six (6) points.
5. Patents — If the original contribution presented in a counted publication results in the granting of
an invention patent in one or more countries, one of the publications from which the patent is
derived may receive an additional 50% of its original points, with a maximum cumulative
total of six (6) additional points.
Coauthorship weightings: First author or corresponding author: 70%, Second author: 50%, Third
author: 30%, Other authors: 10%
Article 6 – Minimum Required Scores
● Assistant Professor: 10 points
● Associate Professor: 12 points
● Professor: 16 points
Applicants promoted to associate professor or professor must have at least one publication that meets
the requirements in point 5 as a first-class publication and be the first author or corresponding author.
For those appointed on or after August 1, 2018, one of the following must apply:
● Two papers meet the requirements of the first-class publications specified in point 5, and the
applicant is the first author or corresponding author.
● One paper meets the requirements of the first-class publications specified in point 5, and the
applicant is the first author or corresponding author; the other paper is a paper presented at a top
international academic conference in the field, and the applicant is the first author or
corresponding author. When submitting the application, a detailed explanation of the reasons and
documentary evidence demonstrating that the acceptance rate of papers at the international

academic conference was 30% or less should be provided. The application must be reviewed
and approved by at least two-thirds of the members present at the departmental academic
evaluation committee and, after approval by the dean, submitted to the faculty academic
evaluation committee for review.
Article 7 – Review Procedures
The review process proceeds as follows:
1. A qualification review will be conducted based on the applicant's relevant documents in
accordance with the "List of Required Documents for Faculty Promotion at this University."
2. If the qualification review meets the requirements, a formal review will be conducted on the
applicant's research, teaching, and service records. The submitted publications will be evaluated
for points according to the provisions of Point 5. The total number of points must meet the
minimum standard for faculty promotion applications at each level as specified in Point 6.
Approval will be obtained from a vote of at least two-thirds of the members of the Faculty
Evaluation Committee present at the meeting before the application is sent to the university for
external review.
3. After passing the formal review, the external review process should be conducted in accordance
with the guidelines for external review of the faculty qualification examination.
4. Upon receiving the external review results, the faculty office should inform the applicant of the
results.
If the external review results are passed, the faculty office should proactively notify the faculty
one week before the faculty evaluation committee meeting for review. The faculty evaluation
committee members may visit the faculty office to review the application materials (research,
teaching, service) and the external review committee's opinions, including other relevant
materials.
5. The Faculty Evaluation Committee shall confirm the credibility and accuracy of the review results
of the academic experts.
If there are five reviewers, applications for promotion to the rank of Professor must receive a total
rating of C or higher from four reviewers, with three of those receiving a rating of B or higher.
Applications for promotion to the rank of Associate Professor or below must receive a total rating
of C or higher from four reviewers, with two of those receiving a rating of B or higher, before
submission to the committee for review. If there are more than five external reviewers, the
standards for submission to the committee for review shall not be lower than the standards
calculated for the five reviewers mentioned above.
6. If the externally reviewed research results are satisfactory and more than two-thirds of the
members present at the Faculty Academic Evaluation Committee vote to approve the scoring of
research, teaching, and service, and the total score of each category reaches 75 points or more,
and the total score of the research projects of more than two-thirds of the members present
reaches 75 points or more, the research project will pass the review and be reported to the
president for final review by the Faculty Academic Evaluation Committee.
The Faculty Office shall inform the applicant for promotion of the results of the Faculty Academic
Evaluation Committee.

7. Any doubts about external review results shall be handled per Article 39 of the Qualification
Review Regulations.
8. Committee members must participate fully; absent members may not vote.
If discussion is postponed, the applicant may be invited to explain in person or in writing before
re-evaluation.
Article 8 – Scoring Criteria
1. Research (50%)
○ Representative publications and reference works (specialized works, works, certificates of
achievement, technical reports).
○ The quality and quantity of papers presented at domestic and international academic
conferences and invited commentaries.
○ The quality and quantity of awards received for publications.
○ The quality and quantity of research projects undertaken.
○ Other research achievements.
2. Teaching (30–40%)
○ Evaluate teaching achievements.
○ Guide and review the quality and quantity of master's and doctoral dissertations.
○ Other activities that promote teaching effectiveness.
○ Members of the Faculty's Academic Evaluation Committee will review the specific
teaching achievement information provided by the departmental (institute, program)
academic evaluation committee and assign scores to each individual. Scores should be
within 10 percent of the departmental (institute, program) academic evaluation
committee's score, and the average score will be calculated.
3. Service (10–20%)
○ Part-time administrative duties related to the university, college, department (institute,
program, office, center), etc.
○ Contributions to department (institute, program, office, center), college, and university
affairs.
○ Serving as an instructor, club, publication advisor, or team advisor.
○ Hosting or co-hosting domestic and international academic seminars.
○ Achievements in social responsibility practices.
○ Achievements in industry-university collaborations.
○ Other service matters.
Members of the college's academic evaluation committee will review the specific service
achievement information provided by the department's (institute, program) academic evaluation
committee and assign scores. Scores should be within 10% of the department's academic
evaluation committee score, and the average score will be calculated.
If the applicant’s scores in Research, Teaching, and Service each reach 75 points or above, and the
weighted average score (calculated according to the prescribed proportions) is also 75 points or above,
the application shall be deemed passing.
The College Faculty Evaluation Committee meeting must be attended by more than one-half of all
members, and promotion shall require the approval of at least two-thirds of the attending members. The
evaluation results, together with the above scores, shall then be submitted to the University Faculty
Evaluation Committee for final deliberation.

Article 8-1 – Flexible Weight Distribution
When applying for promotion, a faculty member may, within the flexible range of proportions specified in
this Article for Teaching and Service, freely determine the percentage allocation (in increments of ten
percent) between the two categories.
If no allocation is chosen, the evaluation proportions shall be set as follows:
Research – 50%, Teaching – 40%, and Service – 10%.
Faculty members who choose to allocate 20% to the Service category must have passed the most
recent faculty performance evaluation and, within seven years after obtaining their previous faculty rank
and prior to submission for review, must meet at least two of the following conditions:
1. Have received the University Outstanding Service Award.
2. Have served as an administrative supervisor or deputy supervisor at the university, college, or
department (institute/program, or university-level center).
3. Have served as editor-in-chief of a major academic journal (SCI(E), SSCI, EI, TSSCI) or another
scholarly journal recognized by the College Faculty Evaluation Committee for at least four
semesters.
4. Have achieved a total accumulated amount of industry–academia collaboration funding of NT$10
million or more.
Article 9
If a promotion application is rejected, the College shall notify the applicant in writing with reasons, and
copy the University and department committees.
The applicant may file an appeal to the University Faculty Grievance Committee within 30 days of
receiving notice.
Article 10
Faculty with higher academic degrees applying for promotion to lecturer or assistant professor shall
undergo external review according to Article 2 (diploma-based review).
Applicants under the old system (assistants or lecturers) must have both thesis and coursework grades
averaging ≥ 80 within seven years.
Article 11
These Key Points are based on Ministry of Education regulations and the University’s Faculty
Appointment and Promotion Evaluation Guidelines. Unspecified matters shall be handled in accordance
with these regulations.
Article 12
These Key Points shall take effect upon approval by the College Affairs Meeting and ratification by the
University Faculty Evaluation Committee. Amendments follow the same procedure.

College) has established these regulations to encourage new faculty members to
promote academic research.

Faculty Members. The recipients of the grant shall be newly appointed full-time faculty
members of the College.

meeting and promulgation by the Dean. The same procedure applies to any
amendments.

Key Points for the External Review Procedures of Faculty
Qualification Evaluation, College of Science, National Chengchi
University
Approved at the 23rd Meeting of the College Faculty Evaluation Committee on October 16, 2001
Filed for record at the 192nd Meeting of the University Faculty Evaluation Committee on January 30,
2002
Amended and approved at the 100th Meeting of the College Faculty Evaluation Committee on October 6,
2011
Amended and approved at the 101st Meeting of the College Faculty Evaluation Committee on November
17, 2011
Filed for record at the 293rd Meeting of the University Faculty Evaluation Committee on December 21,
2011

2013
Filed for record at the 306th Meeting of the University Faculty Evaluation Committee on May 15, 2013
Article 1
The College of Science at National Chengchi University (hereinafter referred to as “the College”)
establishes these Key Points in accordance with the University Guidelines for the External Review of
Faculty Qualification Evaluation, to regulate the procedures for faculty appointment and promotion
qualification reviews within the College.
Article 2
After a faculty appointment or promotion application passes the formal review by the College Faculty
Evaluation Committee (hereinafter “the College Committee”), the Convener of the College Committee
shall assemble a Nomination Subcommittee for External Reviewers (hereinafter “the Nomination
Subcommittee”) consisting of two to three scholars or experts.
Article 3
Within one week after the College Committee’s preliminary approval, the applicant’s department or
institute shall, based on the applicant’s academic specialty and with reference to the applicant’s
submitted lists of reviewers to be recused or excluded (in the format provided in the appendix), submit a
confidential list recommending at least ten external reviewers to the Convener of the College Committee.
The reviewer information shall include the reviewer’s name, current position, academic field, and contact
details (as per the recommendation form format).
Article 4
d
according to the number of reviewers required as specified in Article 3 of the University Guidelines for
External Review Procedures for Faculty Qualification Evaluation.

| The Nomination Subcommittee shall, with reference to the department or institute’s recommended list |
| --- |
| and the applicant’s exclusion list |

External reviewers shall be invited in sequence. The Nomination Subcommittee and all administrative
staff involved shall maintain strict confidentiality.
Article 5
A reviewer must recuse themselves from the review if any of the following conditions apply:
1. The reviewer was the applicant’s thesis or dissertation advisor.
2. The reviewer co-authored any of the applicant’s representative works.
3. The reviewer and the applicant are employed at the same institution.
4. The reviewer has a family relationship with the applicant.
Article 6
Selection of reviewers shall observe the following principles:
1. Reviewers for the same case should not come from the same institution.
2. Reviewers should preferably not be professors from the applicant’s alma mater.
3. Reviewers should preferably not be classmates of the applicant.
4. Reviewers who have previously collaborated with the applicant in relevant research should be
avoided whenever possible.
Article 7
Once the Nomination Subcommittee finalizes the list of reviewers, the College administrative staff shall,
without special reason for delay, contact the reviewers and send the review materials within ten days.
If a contacted reviewer does not respond within three days, the staff may proceed to contact the next
reviewer in the ranked list.
Article 8
The review period shall, in principle, be limited to one month. The College administrative staff shall
remind external reviewers to observe the deadline.
Article 9
During the review process, the College administrative staff shall keep the applicant and their department
(institute or program) informed of the following progress:
1. That all review materials have been sent to the external reviewers.
2. That the external review results have been received by the College.
3. The deliberation results of the College Faculty Evaluation Committee.
Article 10
If the review process cannot be completed on time, the College administrative staff shall apply for an
extension with the University Personnel Office before the end of the semester in which the proposed
promotion is to take effect.

Article 11
Matters not covered in these Key Points shall be handled in accordance with the Ministry of Education’s
Regulations for the Selection of Review Committee Members for Faculty Promotion at Junior Colleges
and Above and the University Guidelines for the External Review of Faculty Qualification Evaluation.
Article 12
These Key Points shall take effect after approval by the College Faculty Evaluation Committee and
submission to the University Faculty Evaluation Committee for record. Amendments shall follow the
same procedure.

Subsidies Encouraging Full-Time Faculty of the College of Science to
Conduct Interdisciplinary Integrated Research Projects, National
Chengchi University
Article 1
The College of Science, National Chengchi University (hereinafter referred to as “the
College”) hereby establishes these regulations to encourage full-time faculty members
of the College to engage in interdisciplinary academic research and to apply for
integrated research projects under the National Science and Technology Council.
Article 2
Full-time faculty members of the College are required to plan interdisciplinary
integrated research projects to apply for this subsidy. Faculty members may submit a
research project concept proposal to the College by the end of October each year. The
proposal will be reviewed in a meeting convened by the Dean with administrative
supervisors, and upon approval, preliminary research will be conducted for a period of
one year.
Article 3
Planning and conducting interdisciplinary integrated research projects:
1. Subsidies under these regulations are granted to projects in which a full-time
faculty member of the College serves as the Principal Investigator.
2. Each integrated project must consist of at least three approved sub-projects in
order to be established. The Principal Investigator of the integrated project
must concurrently serve as the Principal Investigator of one sub-project.
Among the Principal Investigators of the sub-projects, at least three must be
full-time faculty members officially appointed within the College. Other
sub-project Principal Investigators may be affiliated with other colleges or
institutions; however, external members may not exceed one-third of the total
personnel of the integrated project.
3. The sub-projects within an integrated project must belong to at least two
(inclusive) different academic divisions of the National Science and
Technology Council.
4. The research theme of the integrated project shall be determined by the
Principal Investigator. The project must aim to complete preliminary results
within one year and to submit an application for an integrated research project
subsidy to the National Science and Technology Council.
5. Each full-time faculty member officially appointed within the College may
participate in no more than two integrated projects concurrently, and in no
more than two integrated projects within a three-year period.
6. In principle, applications for this subsidy for the same research topic by the
same applicant are limited to a maximum of two submissions. If more than

one-half of the project members are identical, the project shall be deemed the
same integrated project.
Article 4
Subsidized items:
3. Under these regulations, the subsidy for each sub-project shall be capped
at NTD 100,000 and shall be provided for a maximum period of 12 months,
with the subsidy period commencing upon receipt of the approval notification.
Subsidized items include assistant salaries, student wages, domestic and
international travel expenses, and expenses related to the purchase of research
equipment, books, consumables, and other miscellaneous costs directly related
to the project. Principal Investigators of subsidized projects may not receive
remuneration.
4. The maximum subsidy for each integrated project shall not exceed NTD
500,000.
Article 5
Faculty members receiving subsidies shall submit a concise report of no more than ten
pages to the College within one month after the end of the subsidy period. In addition,
during the most recent application period for research project grants accepted by
the National Science and Technology Council, they shall apply to an integrated
research project to the National Science and Technology Council and file a complete
project proposal with the College. If subsidized members fail to apply to an integrated
project to the National Science and Technology Council, none of the project members
shall be eligible to apply for this subsidy for a period of three years.
Article 6
For a second application for subsidy following a previous application for an integrated
project submitted to the National Science and Technology Council that was not
approved, the following items shall be taken into consideration for evaluation:
1. The extent to which the content of the previous research concept has been
completed, or other evidence demonstrating the objectives already achieved by
the project, as well as the improvements made in the current project compared
to the previous proposal.
2. Publications by the College’s Principal Investigator(s) related to the team’s
research theme, published in journals listed in databases such as TSSCI, SCI,
SSCI, and EI, or in academic book chapters or scholarly monographs.
Article 7
The annual subsidy cap under these regulations shall be NTD 1,000,000. Funding
shall be sourced from the College’s administrative and management funds as well as
from internal and external project funding. Expense reimbursement shall be handled
in accordance with relevant university regulations.
Article 8
These regulations shall take effect upon approval by the College Affairs Meeting and
promulgation by the Dean. The regulations shall be implemented on a trial basis for

one year starting from 2020, and may be revised as necessary, following the same
procedures.

Committee”) to handle the nomination and recommendation process. Members
of the College Selection Committee shall be concurrently appointed from among
the members of the College Faculty Evaluation Committee. Any member who is
recommended as a candidate for the College’s Distinguished Teaching Award
shall recuse himself or herself from the review proceedings of meetings for that
academic year.
3. The College Selection Committee shall convene only when more than one-half

consent of more than two-thirds of the members present.

The selection process shall proceed in accordance with the following procedures:

3. The Office of Academic Affairs shall provide a list of courses ranked within

conduct a questionnaire survey on distinguished teaching performance and
provide a list of teachers ranked within the top 50% of each college,
department, and graduate institute, as well as those who have passed the
annual faculty basic performance evaluation.
(2) Stage of Recommendation by the College Selection Committee:
4. Upon receipt of the materials specified in the preceding subparagraph, the

each respective unit for reference.

materials and the following specific criteria, provide supporting
documentation, conduct internal ranking and recommendation, and submit the
list of nominees, recommendation forms, and relevant materials to the College
Selection Committee for review. In principle, each department may
recommend up to two candidates and each graduate institute one candidate:
(1) Demonstration and effective implementation of teaching philosophy with
outstanding results.
(2) Development of instructional materials or teaching websites, innovation in
teaching methods, and compilation and publication as textbooks with excellent
outcomes that serve as references for peers in the same field.
(3) Ability to inspire students’ interest in learning and encourage reading, with
outstanding results.
(4) Provision of regular academic advising and effective encouragement of
student learning.
(5) Excellent teaching performance recognized through peer evaluation; where
necessary, the College may organize a teaching observation panel.
(6) Enhancement of professional competencies with outstanding results.
(7) Distribution of student academic performance.
(8) Effective use of digital instructional materials, teaching websites, and
instructional media.
(9) Supervision of undergraduate research projects under the National Science
and Technology Council and engagement in academia–industry collaboration,
with excellent performance.
(10) Other teaching-related materials.
6. After comprehensive review, the College Selection Committee shall
recommend a number of candidates not exceeding twice the number of
available award positions, rank them accordingly, and submit the
recommendation forms along with supporting documentation to the University
Distinguished Teaching Award Selection Committee for deliberation.
5. In recognition of full-time faculty members of the College who have made
outstanding contributions to teaching,
6. Faculty members who have failed to pass the University’s faculty performance
evaluation and whose results have been duly recorded by the University Faculty
Evaluation Committee shall not be eligible for selection as Distinguished
Teaching Award recipients.

Distinguished Teaching Excellence Award shall not be eligible to participate in

8. Matters not provided for in these Guidelines shall be governed by the
University’s Regulations for the Distinguished Teaching Award and other
applicable laws and regulations.
9. These Guidelines shall be implemented upon approval by the College Affairs
Meeting and submission to the University Selection Committee for recordation;

National Chengchi University College of Science
Regulations for Subsidizing English-Taught Undergraduate Courses
Discussed at the Administrative Supervisors Meeting on October 18, 2017
Amended and Approved at the College Affairs Meeting on December 4, 2017
Article 1
To enhance the quality of English-taught instruction, promote internationalization in teaching, create an
English-speaking learning environment within the College, provide English-taught courses for
undergraduate and international students, and encourage faculty members to teach in English, the
College of Science of National Chengchi University (hereinafter referred to as “the College”) hereby
establishes these Regulations.
Article 2
These subsidies are intended for full-time faculty members of the College. The conditions for subsidies
are as follows:
1. Subsidized Courses: Only newly offered English-taught courses are eligible. Each faculty
member may apply for subsidies for a newly offered course up to two times. The maximum
subsidy for the first application is NT$15,000, and NT$10,000 for the second.
2. Eligible Courses: Only English-taught undergraduate courses are eligible for subsidies.
Article 3
Applications are processed once per semester. Full-time faculty members intending to apply must submit
the English-Taught Course Subsidy Application Form and relevant supporting materials to their
department (institute) before the end of May and the end of December each year, to apply for subsidies
for the following semester.
Article 4
Subsidy applications for English-taught undergraduate courses shall be reviewed by the Administrative
Supervisors Coordination Meeting.
Article 5
The subsidy amount shall be determined based on the following criteria:
1. The primary target students of the English-taught course are undergraduates.
2. The teaching effectiveness of the English-taught course.
3. Plans for future enhancement of the course’s quality.
4. Priority is given to courses included in the College’s English-Taught Program (ETP).
5. Other considerations (e.g., vision, long-term planning).
Article 6
The subsidies provided under these Regulations shall come from the College’s available administrative
funds.
The funds shall be centrally allocated by the College for promoting English-taught instruction and shall
be processed in accordance with relevant regulations based on the funding source. Reimbursement
documents must be submitted before the required deadlines.

Article 7
These Regulations shall be implemented after approval by the College Affairs Meeting and promulgation
by the Dean. The same procedure shall apply to any amendments.

Article 1
The College of Science of National Chengchi University (hereinafter referred to as
“the University” and “the College,” respectively) formulates these Regulations in
order to enhance academic research achievements and to encourage full-time faculty
members within the official staffing establishment to publish papers in domestic and
international journals.
Article 2
Full-time faculty members within the official staffing of the College who publish
papers in journals indexed in SSCI, SCI(E), A&HCI, or EI, and whose institutional
affiliation is indicated as the College (department/institute), shall be awarded a
monetary prize for each paper as encouragement.
However, these Regulations shall not apply to those who, in the same year, have been
selected as Distinguished Chair Professors, Distinguished Professors, Distinguished
Associate Professors, or who have received research awards from the National
Science and Technology Council (hereinafter referred to as the NSTC), academic
research awards from National Chengchi University, or other university-level awards
or subsidies.
The total annual reward per person shall be capped at NT$30,000.
Article 3
Journal articles must have been formally published and appeared in the preceding year
to be eligible for application.
Article 4
If multiple authors co-author an article applying for the award, the award amount shall
be allocated proportionally according to the following weights; however, authors who
do not meet the requirements outlined in Article 2 of these Regulations shall not
receive any award:
70% for the first author or corresponding author,
50% for the second author,

30% for the third author,
and 10% for each of the remaining authors.
Article 5
Applicants shall, before the annually announced deadline, submit the application
form, the first page of the published article, and proof of the journal’s citation index to
the College office to complete the application procedure.
Article 6
Applications shall be reviewed in a meeting convened by the Dean with the
participation of administrative supervisors. The College office shall announce the list
of award recipients. Relevant administrative procedures, including the preparation of
the award disbursement roster, shall be completed before the end of each year, and the
materials, together with the meeting minutes, shall be submitted to the University’s
Office of Research and Development.
Article 7
The funding required for these Regulations shall be supported by self-generated
revenues of the University Endowment Fund. The annual award amount allocated to
the College shall be calculated in accordance with Article 4 of the National Chengchi
University Regulations Governing Incentives for Academic Research.
Article 8
These Regulations shall be implemented upon approval by the College Affairs

National Chengchi University
College of Science
Regulations for Flexible Teaching Hours for Full-Time Faculty Members
Approved at the 13th Meeting of the College Curriculum Committee on May 11, 2018
Approved at the 112th and 113th College Affairs Meetings on October 1 and December 3, 2018
Article 5 amended and approved at the 16th Meeting of the College Curriculum Committee on May 20,
2019

Amended and approved at the 17th Meeting of the College Curriculum Committee on October 16, 2019
Paragraph 1 of Article 5 amended and approved at the 115th College Affairs Meeting on October 28,
2019
Articles 2 to 8 amended and approved at the 21st Meeting of the College Curriculum Committee on May
26, 2020
Articles 2 to 8 amended and approved at the 119th College Affairs Meeting on June 8, 2020
Article 2 amended and approved at the 27th Meeting of the College Curriculum Committee on October
20, 2022
Article 2 amended and approved at the 128th College Affairs Meeting on December 26, 2022
Article 1
The College of Science of National Chengchi University (hereinafter referred to as “the College”)
establishes these Regulations to align with the University’s Curriculum Streamlining Initiative and to
implement flexible teaching-hour measures, allowing adjustments based on faculty members’ teaching or
research focus.
Article 2
Full-time faculty members of the College who, in the current academic year or in the preceding two
consecutive academic years, have served as Principal Investigators of research projects funded by the
National Science and Technology Council (NSTC) (hereinafter referred to as “NSTC”) or research
projects of equivalent status domestically or internationally (Note 1), shall have a basic teaching load of
12 hours in the following academic year.
Newly appointed full-time faculty members shall have a basic teaching load of 12 hours per academic
year.
Full-time faculty members concurrently holding administrative positions shall have their basic teaching
load determined in accordance with the University’s Curriculum Streamlining Initiative and related
regulations.
Full-time faculty members who have reached the age of 62 shall, starting that academic year, have a
basic teaching load set at 12 hours in principle.
Faculty members who do not meet the above criteria shall have a basic teaching load of 15 hours.
Article 3

In principle, the reduced teaching load for full-time faculty members shall not exceed 3 hours per
academic year.
For faculty members on sabbatical, secondment, approved overseas research leave, or extended
medical leave for one semester, both the required teaching hours and the allowable reduced teaching
hours shall be calculated at half.
Article 4
Each academic year, the College shall calculate the total allowable reduction hours by multiplying the
number of faculty members with a basic teaching load of 15 hours (as defined in Article 2) by 3 hours.
The total reduction hours shall then be allocated according to the reduction categories and priority order
listed in Article 5.
Article 5
Reduction categories and their priority order for full-time faculty members are as follows:
1. Newly appointed full-time faculty members may apply for reduced teaching hours within their
first two academic years, up to 3 hours per academic year. However, the reduced hours must
be compensated by other full-time faculty members of the College.
2. Special reductions for assisting with College or departmental administrative affairs or other
designated tasks may be granted, upon approval by the Dean, for up to 3 hours per academic
year.
However, the total teaching load shall not fall below 12 hours per academic year.
Reduced hours under the above categories may not be carried over for later use, except where required
for departmental teaching needs.
Article 6
Departments and institutes shall offer courses at the undergraduate, master’s, and doctoral levels
according to planned instructional needs, ensuring sufficient courses for students to meet graduation
requirements.
Departments and institutes shall avoid imbalances between course offerings in fall and spring semesters,
and should comply with the College’s requirement that course offerings in the two semesters maintain
90% consistency.
Any matters not covered in these Regulations shall be handled in accordance with the University’s
Curriculum Streamlining Initiative and related NCCU regulations.
Article 7
These Regulations shall take effect upon approval by both the College Curriculum Committee and the
College Affairs Meeting, and promulgation by the Dean. The same procedure applies to any
amendments.

College of Science Academic Journal Publication Subsidy
Regulations, National Chengchi University
Approved at the 115th College Affairs Meeting on October 28, 2019 (entire text initially approved)
Amended at the 116th College Affairs Meeting on December 2, 2019 (Articles 2, 3, and 6)
Approved at the 117th College Affairs Meeting on February 17, 2020
Amended at the 128th College Affairs Meeting on December 26, 2022 (Article 3, including the
Appendix, and Article 11)
Article 1
The College of Science, National Chengchi University (hereinafter referred to as “the
College”), in order to encourage outstanding academic research performance by
full-time faculty members, hereby promulgates these Regulations.
Article 2
Subsidies for academic journal publications shall be administered once each academic
year, with an application deadline of April 1. Eligible applications shall be limited
to academic articles that were accepted for publication or published within one year
prior to the application deadline, and that are published under the affiliation “National
Chengchi University.”
The following shall not be eligible for subsidy: correspondence, review, book review,
correct, reply, editorial, and other non-academic articles.
Article 3
Subsidies for academic journal publications of the College shall be determined
through the complementary application of two evaluation criteria—tiering based on
Impact Factor and tiering based on journal rankings within respective disciplines.
Applicants may freely choose either criterion. The classification standards, subsidy
amounts, and disbursement methods are outlined in the table below:

| Category | Description of Subsidy Items | Maximum Subsidy Amount per Article (NTD) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| (I) | Articles published in top-tier SCI/SSCI journals with an Impact Factor of 30 or higher | NT$300,000 |
| (II) | Articles published in top-tier SCI/SSCI journals with an Impact Factor of 20 or higher | NT$200,000 |
| (III) | Articles published in top-tier SCI/SSCI journals with an Impact Factor of 10 or higher | NT$100,000 |
| (IV) | Articles published in SCI/SSCI journals ranked within the top 1% of their respective disciplines according to the latest Journal Citation Reports (JCR), or articles in international journals or international | NT$70,000 |

Note 1: For subsidy categories (IV) and (V), the list of international journals and
international conferences of equivalent standing is provided in the appendix.
Note 2: In principle, a single article that has already received other funding or
subsidies from the University or the College shall not be eligible for duplicate or
concurrent subsidies.
Article 4
Full-time faculty members affiliated with the College who have served for at least one
year and have published articles under the affiliation “National Chengchi
University” may apply to the College for subsidies.
For co-authored articles, scores shall be calculated using weighted allocation: 70% for
the first author or corresponding author, and 10% for other authors. Only one
applicant may submit a subsidy application for the same article.
If the order of authorship is not determined by contribution, applicants shall provide
a statement explaining individual contributions along with documentation of the
proportional ranking.
For jointly appointed full-time faculty members, those whose primary appointment
unit is the College shall be subject to the College’s subsidy principles for full-time
faculty.
Article 5
Recipients of the subsidy shall provide a Chinese abstract of the published
article and agree to participate in related interviews, as necessary, to assist in the
promotion of science communication and public outreach.
Article 6
Applicants for academic journal publication subsidies shall submit the following
documents:
(1) The full text of the article.
(2) For published articles, a photocopy of the table of contents of the journal issue in
which the article was published.
(3) For articles that have been accepted but not yet published, an official letter of
acceptance.
(4) Supporting documentation for the applied article, including journal ranking tier,
impact factor, and other relevant evidentiary materials.

|  | conference proceedings of equivalent standing Note 1 |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| (V) | Articles published in SCI/SSCI journals ranked within the top 1–25% of their respective disciplines according to the latest Journal Citation Reports (JCR), or articles in international journals or international conference proceedings of equivalent standing Note 1 | NT$20,000 |

(5) A preliminary review and confirmation form issued by the applicant’s affiliated
department (or program).
Article 7
After applications have undergone preliminary review by the respective departments
(programs), the Dean shall convene a meeting of administrative supervisors to
conduct the review. Applications shall then be reviewed and ranked in accordance
with the following principles:
(1) Within the same category of articles, ranking shall begin with applicants of shorter
academic seniority, in the order of Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, and
Professor.
For applicants holding the same academic rank, ranking priority shall be determined
by length of service at the College of Science, with those of shorter service receiving
priority.
(2) Among all applications submitted by applicants at the same rank, one application
with the highest requested subsidy amount from each applicant shall first be included
in the ranking.
After each applicant has been ranked once, the next highest-amount application from
the same applicant shall be considered, and so forth.
Article 7
After applications have undergone preliminary review by the respective departments
(programs), the Dean shall convene a meeting of administrative supervisors to
conduct the review. Applications shall then be reviewed and ranked in accordance
with the following principles:
(1) Within the same category of articles, ranking shall begin with applicants of shorter
academic seniority, in the order of Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, and
Professor.
For applicants holding the same academic rank, ranking priority shall be determined
by length of service at the College of Science, with those of shorter service receiving
priority.
(2) Among all applications submitted by applicants at the same rank, one application
with the highest requested subsidy amount from each applicant shall first be included
in the ranking.
After each applicant has been ranked once, the next highest-amount application from
the same applicant shall be considered, and so forth.
(3) Journal Impact Factors shall be determined based on the values listed in the
Journal Citation Reports (JCR) database for the year of application.
If the Impact Factor for the application year is not yet available, the most recent prior
year’s data shall be applied, with retrospective reference limited to a maximum of
three years.

Article 8
The annual subsidy budget and the maximum subsidy amount per applicant shall each
be NT$600,000.
If the total approved subsidy amounts exceed the available budget for any
category, priority shall be given to newly appointed faculty members.
Article 9
If an applicant is found to have violated these Regulations or other applicable laws or
regulations, the Committee may revoke the subsidy and demand full reimbursement
of the subsidized funds.
The applicant shall bear all related expenses, including income tax and supplementary
premiums for the Second-Generation National Health Insurance (both the individual
and employer portions).
Article 10
Funding for these Regulations shall be derived from the College of Science Program
for Enhancing Academic Research Outcomes, the College’s administrative
management fees, and internal and external subsidy or grant funds.
Article 11
These Regulations shall be promulgated and implemented by the Dean upon approval
by the College Affairs Meeting. The same shall apply to any amendments thereto.

National Chengchi University Regulations on the Establishment of Research Awards for Young
Scholars in the College of Science
Adopted at the 89th College Affairs Meeting on November 25, 2013
Amended at the 104th College Affairs Meeting on September 12, 2016 (Article 3)
Amended at the 131st College Affairs Meeting on December 25, 2023 (Articles 6 and 7)
Article 1 To encourage young faculty members of the College of Science, National Chengchi
University (hereinafter referred to as “the College”), to actively engage in academic
research and pursue excellence, these Regulations are hereby established.
Article 2 Full-time faculty members within the College who have served for at least one year
and are aged 45 or below, holding the rank of Assistant Professor or Associate
Professor (hereinafter referred to as “Young Scholars”), may be recommended by
their department or institute to apply. After being reviewed and approved by the
College, related procedures shall be processed accordingly.
Article 3 The College establishes the “Young Scholar Research Award” to recognize
full-time faculty members of the University who have made substantial academic
research contributions and who, within the past three years, meet one or more of the
following criteria:
1. Conducted pioneering or interdisciplinary research with concrete contributions.
2. Published scholarly monographs of significant academic impact.
3. Collaborated with industry to transfer research outcomes (e.g., patents,
inventions, or technologies) that have produced demonstrable achievements.
4. Produced research outcomes contributing to the resolution of major social
issues with outstanding performance.
5. Achieved substantial recognition from the international academic community
for research contributions.
6. Published a considerable number of high-quality research papers with
excellent outcomes.
Article 4 Up to three young scholars may be selected each year for the award. The research
achievements and award results shall be publicly announced by the College for
reference by the University and the general public.
Article 5 Each department or institute shall submit nominations with the following documents:
a letter of recommendation, an application form, relevant supporting materials
(including curriculum vitae, publication list, major works, and evidence of specific
achievements), to the College for processing.
Article 6 The College shall conduct the review process as follows:
1. The application materials of the recommended candidates shall be submitted
to the College Distinguished Professor and Associate Professor
Selection Committee (hereinafter “College Selection Committee”) by the end
of May each year for review assistance.
2. The College Selection Committee meeting must be attended by at least
two-thirds of its members. A candidate shall be approved with the consent of
two-thirds (inclusive) of the attending members. If more than three applicants
receive approval, the Committee shall rank them by priority and submit the list

to the Dean for final approval.
Article 7 The award shall be presented publicly, with each recipient receiving a “Young
Scholar Research Award” plaque and a research grant of NT$100,000 as
recognition. The research grant shall be funded by the Higher Education Sprout
Project budget of the College. If funds are insufficient, the balance shall be covered
by the College’s administrative budget. Expenditures shall comply with the relevant
regulations of the Higher Education Sprout Project and the University.
Article 8 Recipients of this award shall not reapply within three years of receiving it.
Article 9 These Regulations shall take effect after approval by the College Affairs Meeting. The
same procedure applies to any amendments.
